what: differential: every input decodes to a world (size, food grid, fertility, creatures, actions) that is stepped by the C kernel, the C kernel with the asm crowd scan, and the Rust kernel; sensors, births/deaths and full state must agree bit for bit after every tick, and positions/headings/sensors must stay in range
sanitizers: -fsanitize=fuzzer,address,undefined,float-cast-overflow -fno-sanitize-recover=all (C kernel and harness instrumented; asm and the Rust staticlib are checked differentially but are not coverage-instrumented)
host: 8 vCPU Intel Xeon container, Linux, single fuzzing process

findings.what: worlds smaller than 3 grid cells (24 units) per axis: collision pushes can leave the torus after one wrap step and the 3x3 neighbourhood aliases (crowding double-counted). All backends agreed, so it was a spec gap, not a backend mismatch.
findings.fix: World.new rejects w/h < 72 (and NaN/inf/huge sizes, bad food cell, bad capacity) on every backend; the harness now only generates legal worlds. Real runs use 768x512 and were unaffected (tools/reproduce.rb still matches bit for bit).

note: coverage plateaued at 188 edges within the first few hundred execs: the kernel is branch-light, so most of the value is the differential and sanitizer checks over 4.3M random worlds, not new coverage
